instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Alissa is on holiday with her parents. In the morning, when her parents are still asleep, she has the pool all to herself. She decides to go swimming.

atoms.a: Why is it dangerous for Alissa to go swimming by herself?
b: ++Because no one can help her if she has problems in the water.
Because no one sees how far she can dive.
Because swimming alone is not fun.

instruction.text: Select the picture where the situation is no longer dangerous for Alissa.

feedback.end: Great! The person supervising could be a lifeguard or an adult you know.

atoms.text: Cara is at the beach with her uncle. She runs to the water without telling him.
He is so engrossed in his book that he doesn’t see her jumping into the sea.

atoms.a: How does Cara look? There is more than one correct answer.
b: ++Cara looks like she can no longer keep herself above water.
Cara looks like she’s having a lot of fun in the water.

feedback.end: If you are struggling, it is important to try and wave both hands.

atoms.text: Cara has a cramp in her leg and needs help. Her uncle hasn’t noticed yet because he didn’t see her go into the water.

instruction.text: What must we do before going swimming? Select the two correct answers.

b: ++Let someone responsible know that we are going into the water.
Sneak away from the people we are with.

instruction.text: Decide which of these actions are permitted and which are prohibited at swimming pools.

feedback.end: It is very dangerous to run near a pool because it is often slippery and wet.
Holding someone under water is very dangerous. It could make them panic or drown.

trainers.finishSound: I am considerate, I do not run, push or hold anyone underwater.
